name: Neiman Marcus Cookies
desc: Chocolate chip cookies made tender with blended oats and loaded with walnuts and a chopped milk chocolate bar.

source.title: Neiman Marcus Cookies
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line baking sheets with parchment.
Blend the oats in a blender until they are a fine powder.
In a bowl, whisk the oat flour, all-purpose flour, salt, baking powder and baking soda.
In a stand mixer, beat the butter, granulated sugar and brown sugar on medium-high until light and fluffy, 2-3 min.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Add the dry mixture and mix on low until about half combined.
Add the chocolate chips, chopped milk chocolate and walnuts, and fold by hand until no dry flour remains.
Roll into balls (about 2 tbsp each for regular cookies) and space them 2 in apart on the sheets.
Bake 10-15 min depending on size, until lightly browned at the edges and just set in the center.
Cool 5 min on the sheet, then move to a rack.
tips: Blended oats give a tender, nutty texture.
The reel lists no salt. Barbara Bakes and The Girl Who Ate Everything both use 1/2 tsp, added here; skip it if you bake with salted butter.
Both published versions bake regular-size cookies 8-12 min at 375°F; the reel's longer time is for bigger scoops.
